title: A routine
text: Somewhere between the tenth and twentieth evening, the house acquires habits. The kettle goes on before either of you asks, and the coffee drips through the phin at its own unhurried pace. On Sunday you walk to the bakery at the corner and return with rolls that are still warm and a small argument about which ones to buy. Shoes pile up by the door in a way that would be untidy anywhere else. Nobody announces any of this. You simply notice one morning that the house knows its own rhythm, and that you do too.
